findings.highlight: I release the depression in my lungs.
findings.evidenceJa: 肺にたまった憂鬱を吐き出す
findings.governingReading: His sigh figuratively expels the melancholy accumulated in his lungs.
findings.explanation: The dictionary-near English treats an embodied metaphor as literal clinical “depression” and produces unnatural prose.

findings.evidenceJa: 自分に都合のいい妄想
findings.governingReading: He rebukes himself for believing a self-serving delusion or fantasy.
findings.explanation: The English changes self-deception through fantasy into an unspecified act of deception.

findings.highlight: will get really mad before she laughs at me
findings.evidenceJa: 笑い飛ばされる前に本気で怒られそうだ
findings.governingReading: He imagines Rin seriously scolding him before she could simply laugh the absurdity off.
findings.explanation: The English turns dismissive laughter at the idea into ridicule directed at Shirou.

findings.highlight: if she saw me like this
findings.evidenceJa: こんなとこ、遠坂に見られたら
findings.governingReading: If Rin were to see him like this, he imagines how she would react.
findings.explanation: “I bet Tohsaka will … if she saw” combines incompatible future and past forms.

findings.highlight: I have other things to worry about.
findings.evidenceJa: 悩むならもっと別のことを考えろ
findings.governingReading: He commands himself that if he is going to worry, he should think about something else.
findings.explanation: The English removes the conditional self-command and replaces it with a plain statement of competing concerns.

findings.governingReading: He does not know how the arm’s dull ache will develop.
findings.explanation: The English again removes the pain’s location and dull quality.
